subject: Food Science
title: Gas-Producing Bacteria
description: Learn Gas-Producing Bacteria in one minute.

hook.text: A swollen can of tuna means gas is building up inside. Bacteria are feasting and their waste is pressurizing the can.

buildup.text: Certain bacteria produce CO₂ or hydrogen gas as metabolic byproducts. In sealed containers, pressure builds up.

discovery.text: Clostridium species are notorious gas producers. In canned food, their gas signals potential botulism toxin.

twist.text: Not all gas is bad. CO₂ from lactic acid bacteria creates the holes in Swiss cheese—entirely intentional.

climax.text: Blown packaging is a red flag in food safety. Never taste food from a swollen or bulging container.

punchline.text: Bulging can? Don't open it. The bacteria already told you something's wrong.

quiz.question: What does a swollen food can indicate?
options: Bacteria are producing gas—potentially dangerous toxins may be present
